items.title: Air India Names Ethiopian Airlines’ Former CEO to Lead Turnaround
items.summary: Tewolde Gebremariam coming in as Air India CEO was definitely not in our bingo card, but it may be exactly the kind of operator the airline needs for its next phase.

items.title: What IndiGo and Ethiopian Say About the Rise of the Rest
items.summary: IndiGo and Ethiopian Airlines were built on workers, traders, students, and diaspora travel rather than tourism. Destinations that understand those flows will spend their money differently.

items.title: Can Banks Become the New Hotel Tastemakers? Capital One Travel Thinks So
items.summary: Capital One Travel built its business around how people actually travel. Its Premier and Lifestyle Collections bring that strategy to lodging, helping premium travelers navigate a growing range of options through more thoughtful discovery and curation.

items.title: Wynn’s UAE Casino Is Delayed and Costlier — CEO Calls It a ‘Monopoly’ Worth the Spend
items.summary: Despite a $600 million overrun, Wynn doubled down on the UAE — treating regional conflict as a cost, not a reason to pause.

items.title: Faye Raises $50 Million, Bets on AI to Get Travel Insurance Claims Paid in Minutes
items.summary: Faye is using AI to move more claims from filing to payment while keeping denials with humans. That makes the claims experience, not just the checkout offer, the core of its pitch to travel brands.

items.title: Booking Holdings CEO: AI Overviews Are Squeezing SEO
items.summary: No travel business has found the silver bullet yet in how to show up prominently on a consistent basis within the major LLMs. As these platforms evolve, such an achievement becomes a moving target.

items.title: One Airline Is Carrying the Lufthansa Group – It Isn’t Lufthansa
items.summary: As the German group prepares to double down in Rome and potentially Lisbon, the challenge isn’t finding new hubs – it's getting them to perform more like Swiss in Zurich.

items.title: Iran War Drags Down Q2 Earnings for Big Hotel Chains
items.summary: Q2 came in better than feared across the board, thanks to resilient domestic demand. But no one’s calling it over — Q4, the Gulf’s peak season, is the real test.
